key_insight: Optical imaging combined with Bayesian inference can localize perovskite solar cell degradation to specific interfaces versus the bulk, revealing where device failure begins.
engineering_relevance: This enables targeted materials and interface engineering, including passivation strategies, to improve stability and lifetime in perovskite solar cells.
method: Photoluminescence imaging was paired with drift-diffusion simulations of fully fabricated devices.
Bayesian inference produced spatially resolved inferred maps of recombination-related parameters.
Parameter maps were tracked over aging under 70 °C full-spectrum sunlight to separate electron/hole interface and bulk degradation.
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated by tracking temporal evolution of inferred parameter maps during accelerated aging and showed pronounced spatial heterogeneity, with the strongest degradation localized at perovskite/transport-layer interfaces.
watch_item: Inference quality depends on the accuracy of the drift-diffusion model and imaging data, so mis-specified physics or limited spatial resolution could bias the degradation attribution.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
